title: Phthalate Profiles in High-Fat Dairy Products and Primary Packaging from Almaty, Kazakhstan
content: This study investigates seven phthalate esters (PAEs) in high-fat dairy products (sour cream, cheese, butter) and their primary packaging from the Kazakhstani retail market, alongside a dietary risk assessment. Using a validated, fat-normalized QuEChERS-GC-MS method, dual-matrix analysis evaluated the transfer interface. Dibutyl phthalate (DBP) dominated all categories, reaching up to 24 169.5 µg kg⁻¹ in butter, a level up to 200-fold the EU specific migration limit, among the highest reported globally. DEHP did not follow the fat-content gradient, peaking instead in sour cream (916.0 µg kg⁻¹), suggesting contamination beyond primary packaging. Packaging showed non-proportional PAE transfer, with critical burdens in multilayer carton board. Children were most vulnerable: the cumulative Hazard Index for anti-androgenic PAEs reached 0.41 for cheese consumption alone. These findings indicate a high PAE contamination burden in the Almaty market and highlight the need for PAE-specific monitoring, though as a single-city survey, findings are not nationally representative.
